https://en.shafaqna.com/471942/head-of-i.text: Afghanistan Arabic Azerbaijan Bahrain French India Iraq Lebanon Pakistan Persian Shia News Spanish Turkish Urdu Russian Neshan About / Contact Us Shafaqna English- Iran’s seminaries and the Romanian Orthodox Church have signaled a new phase of interfaith cooperation. Head of Iran’s Islamic Seminaries, Ayatollah Alireza Arafi, in his message, highlighted deep commonalities between Shia Islam and Orthodox Christianity, particularly in core beliefs, mysticism, and moral teachings. He underlined the need for God-centered dialogue as a response to the moral and spiritual crises facing modern societies. The letter was handed over by Hojatoleslam Amin-Din, director of the Office of Religions and Denominations of the Islamic Seminaries, to Dr. Valentin Ilie, the Romanian Orthodox Church’s coordinator for interfaith dialogue. Citing verses from the Quran and the Gospel, Ayatollah Arafi pointed to shared concerns over the weakening of the family institution and the spread of religious disengagement among youth. He described the teachings of both faiths on protecting the family and raising faithful generations as common ground for academic and research cooperation. The message also paid tribute to Saint Mary (PBUH) and other revered figures, urging that they be presented as role models for younger generations. Ayatollah Arafi announced Iran’s full readiness to cooperate with the Romanian Orthodox Church in educational, research, religious, cultural, and social fields. Proposed areas include exchanging professors and researchers, particularly in ethics, organizing international conferences on family and spirituality, and sharing experiences in religious affairs. The initiative follows a series of recent interfaith webinars and scientific meetings between Iranian and Romanian religious and academic figures, organized with the participation of Iranian seminaries, Romanian universities, and the Orthodox Church. Ayatollah Arafi expressed hope that broader cooperation with the Romanian Orthodox Church would serve as an effective step toward promoting spirituality and morality worldwide, praying for the health and happiness of Patriarch Daniel and all Christians. Beállítom Összehangolt európai választ sürgetett a drogcsempész-hálózatok ellen az Európai Parlament (EP) csütörtöki határozata. A testület közleménye szerint a jogi következmények nélküli szöveg a kikötők erősebb védelmét és több információ megosztását szeretné. Több tagállami és uniós pénzt fordítana a bűnüldözésre. Az uniós rendőrségi (Europol), igazságügyi (Eurojust), határvédelmi (Frontex) ügynökségeknek, valamint az Európai Tengerészeti Biztonsági Ügynökségnek fokoznia kellene a közös akciókat. Az EU-n kívüli országokkal is jobban együtt kellene dolgozni, például a nyugat-afrikaiakkal a csempészet, Kínával a drogok gyártásához szükséges anyagok ellen. A képviselők üdvözölték, hogy az Európai Bizottság tavaly decemberben kiadott egy drogstratégiát. Befektetéseket szorgalmaztak, hogy kezeljék a csempészethez vezető társadalmi és gazdasági okokat. A képviselők 601 igennel, négy nem és öt tartózkodás mellett szavazták meg az állásfoglalást. A jegyzőkönyv szerint az ellenzők között volt egy német viccpárti , két görög kommunista , valamint egy lengyel képviselő. Utóbbi, Grzegorz Braun korábban számos botrányba keveredett, például tűzoltókészülékkel fújta le a varsói parlamentben felállított menórát, majd közölte, hogy a hanuka sátáni ünnep, ő pedig csak a normalitást állítja helyre. Más alkalommal egy nyilvános beszélgetésen egy holokausztkutató mikrofonját tette tönkre. Oroszpártiságát illusztrálja, hogy egyszer egy karácsonyfát is kukába dobott, mert az az EU és Ukrajna sárga-kék színeivel volt feldíszítve. Tavaly az EP egy magyar áldozat lányával emlékezett meg a holokausztról, ebbe üvöltözött bele többször, még az egyperces néma csend alatt is Braun. Végül Roberta Metsola EP-elnök megelégelte a viselkedését és kivezettette a teremből. ( Itt írtunk Braunról bővebben.) Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Composite: NSW police/Network 10 New South Wales Bullet hole in door and DNA evidence scrutinised in Beau Lamarre-Condon double murder trial Defence also cross-examines witness over postmortem examinations of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kat Wong Mon 12 Oct 2026 22.52 EDT Last modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 23.16 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A bullet hole left in a bedroom door and DNA found in the barrel of the firearm have been scrutinised in court as Beau Lamarre-Condon’s double murder trial continues in Sydney . Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in on 19 February 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter. The prosecution argues the policeman disguised himself as an UberEats rider before entering Baird’s home, shooting him twice – in the base of the neck and the right temple – and then shooting Davies through the bedroom door. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email But the defence alleges they were killed in two separate incidents when Lamarre-Condon was acting in “self-defence”. During the tussle with Baird, the firearm was flung across the room where it was picked up by Davies, who later shot himself in a struggle with the policeman, the defence argues. Defence lawyer John Stratton SC cross-examined crime scene officer Greg Moon on Tuesday, questioning the prosecution’s version of events. Stratton pointed to a swab taken from the barrel of the alleged murder weapon, which returned a DNA profile that partially matched Davies. He then noted the hole in the bedroom door, through which the prosecution alleges Davies was shot, tested negative for blood. Stratton suggested: “The possibility or likelihood of biological material finding its way from a wound of the deceased through a hole in the door less than a centimetre in width and into the barrel of a gun … approaches zero.” But Moon told the New South Wales supreme court he disagreed. “I believe it can still happen,” he said. The defence does not dispute the couple were shot. View image in fullscreen A bullet hole in the door of Jesse Baird’s bedroom. Photograph: NSW police/Provided by NSW supreme court A diagram from Dr Kendall Bailey, who conducted the postmortem examinations of both men, suggested a bullet entered Baird’s body at the base of his neck and exited just below his lip. Asked by crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC about the effect of this wound, Bailey told the jury it did not pass through any major vessels of the neck or the vertebral column or windpipe. But that did not mean it was insignificant, the court heard. “It still would be a very nasty injury and that fracturing of the jaw is a very nasty injury,” she told the court. While it is potentially survivable, those kinds of injuries can be painful and cause some to pass out, though others may not lose consciousness, Bailey explained. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Hatfield then asked if person with those injuries could speak. The bullet went through the jaw and the base of the tongue, Bailey said, adding: “I don’t think anyone with that injury would be making any meaningful vocalisations. “They could make a noise but that would be nothing that would be coherent,” she said. Bailey then explained the shot that entered the temple would go through the brain, where it would incapacitate a person. Asked if that person would then be able to fling a gun to the other side of the room, she said the body could make some involuntary movements but “I don’t think that person is making any conscious movements”. CT scans of Baird and Davies’ skulls showing the damage caused by the bullets were presented to the jury on Thursday. Forensic radiologist Dr James Raleigh explained to the court there was a hole in the right side of Baird’s head at the temple region and multiple small bone fragments “presumably from that damage were run in a line across the inside of the skull”. Davies’ wound was located in his face just above the left eyebrow, which Raleigh agreed was consistent with a bullet hole. Two wounds on Davies’ thigh were consistent with a “single-bladed weapon”, Bailey said. But she agreed those injuries likely took place after or at the time of death. The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues. https://www.rte.ie/news/2026/1027/159701.text: Updated / Wednesday, 28 Oct 2026 07:25 Daniel Simion Toader was remanded in custody to appear in court again next Tuesday (Pic: Collins) Aisling Kenny By Aisling Kenny A 47-year-old man appeared in court yesterday charged with the murder of his partner, whose body was found in Finglas in Dublin on Monday morning. Daniel Simion Toader, a Romanian national, appeared before Dublin District Court, charged with the murder of 48-year-old Loredana Morosanu at their home at Melville Terrace. Emergency services were called to the house at 4.30am yesterday and found Ms Morosanu. The pharmacy worker, who was originally from Romania but had lived in Ireland for several years, was pronounced dead at the scene. Loredana Morosanu was found at her home in Finglas on Monday morning The accused stood with his hands in his pockets at the start of the two-minute hearing. He then sat and spoke only to a court-appointed interpreter. He had no legal representation in court. Most criminal law solicitors in Dublin have withdrawn their services in response to legal aid payment reforms introduced in July, causing widespread disruption to the criminal justice system. Detective Sergeant Niall Murray gave evidence of arrest, charge and caution to the court. He told the court that the accused was arrested and charged yesterday evening at Finglas Garda Station and he made no reply to the charge. Judge Máire Connelly remanded him in custody to appear again via video link at Cloverhill District Court next Tuesday, 3 November.
